newsitem.title: USA: Ill. governor says campaign finance reform needed.
newsitem.headline: Ill. governor says campaign finance reform needed.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar on Wednesday called for continued campaign finance reform that would require "full identification" of contributors.
In his state of the state address, the Republican governor said a contributor's occupation and employer should be required along with their name.
He also proposed raising the reporting threshold to $250 contributions from the current $150 and moving the state primary from March to a later month.
Edgar also pressed lawmakers to consider deregulation of the electric utility industry, saying the move would increase competition and provide rate relief.
At the top of his address, Edgar pronounced the state's economy to be "solid, diverse, productive, vibrant and expanding."
He said the state has eliminated a more than $1 billion backlog in Medicaid bills, is paying its bills on time and has balanced its budget.
"We find ourselves in a very good fiscal situation today because we had the discipline to tighten our belts, to overcome what was a very bad fiscal situation just a few years ago," Edgar said.

Illinois' poor financial shape led to five general obligation rating downgrades by Standard & Poor's Corp and Moody's Investors Service since 1991. Both rating agencies currently have positive outlooks on the state's rating.
